survey: A retro fuel pump seen in three-quarter view from the front left. The main body is a rounded upright box standing on a flat grey plinth, which rests flat on a concrete slab. A short grey neck rises from the top of the body and carries a flat red-and-white sign box, centred on the neck. The front face has a counter window with five digits, two small knobs and a slot, and below it a round dial gauge with a needle. The gauge's 0.82 width ratio and horizontal short axis fit a front face turned slightly away from the viewer, the same turn as the counter window. The right side has a recessed holster. The orange nozzle hangs in it with its spout tucked into the top of the recess. The hose leaves the holster recess at its lower end (grey section), drops down beside the body, loops at the bottom and rises as the black section into the grey collar at the base of the nozzle handle. So the hose has a real attachment at both ends. The tool marks broken hose segments only where the colour changes from grey to black, not real breaks. The grey patches at the base of the body are worn paint, not structure.
